memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and all living creatures of every kind on the earth." - Gen 9:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is a tender surprise in this verse. God says the rainbow is not only for us to see, but for Him: "I will see it and remember." Of course, God never actually forgets - He does not need a reminder the way we do. But He speaks in this warm, personal way to assure us how committed He is to His promise. He so binds Himself to His covenant that He describes Himself looking at the rainbow and remembering it.

What comfort this gives! The keeping of the covenant does not depend on us remembering, being faithful, or holding up our end. It depends on God, who "remembers" His everlasting promise. Our security rests not on the strength of our grip on God, but on the strength of His grip on us.

This is the heart of grace. God takes responsibility for keeping His promises. When our faith is weak and our memory of His goodness fades, God has not forgotten. He remembers His covenant when we forget it. He is faithful even when we are faithless, "for he cannot disown himself" (2 Tim 2:13).

The everlasting covenant finds its fulfilment in Christ, through whom God has made promises that can never fail. Because God remembers His covenant, you are secure. Your standing before Him does not rest on your shaky remembering but on His unfailing faithfulness. Rest today in the God who never forgets His promises to His people.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does your security rest on your faithfulness, or on God's?
- How does it comfort you that God takes responsibility to remember His promises?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that keeping Your covenant depends on You, not on me. When my faith is weak and my memory fades, thank You that You remember Your promises. My security rests in Your unfailing faithfulness.
